title: Venus Williams given US Open singles wildcard - will Serena join her?
description: Venus Williams is given a wildcard for the US Open singles aged 46 - and 29 years after she made her New York debut.
fullText:
Venus Williams has been given a wildcard for the US Open singles - and sister Serena could potentially still join her with one spot remaining.

Venus, 46, first played in New York 29 years ago and reached the final on her singles debut in 1997.

The American won two of her seven Grand Slam singles titles at Flushing Meadows in 2000 and 2001.

Venus and 2017 champion Sloane Stephens have been given direct entry into the main draw which begins on Sunday, 30 August.

Serena returned to tennis in June, four years after "evolving away" from the sport, and played in singles at Wimbledon.

The sisters were due to play doubles together at SW19 but withdrew after Serena, 44, injured her knee in her first-round loss to Maya Joint.

They made their return together at the Cincinnati Open on Tuesday, losing a thriller at the Cincinnati Open in three sets.

Wildcards for the women's doubles have yet to be announced, and there are three remaining places in the revamped mixed doubles competition that takes place from 24 August.

Elder sister Venus has played singles sporadically on the WTA Tour over the past four years but has lost all 10 of her matches this season and is winless in 13.

Her last singles win was in Washington in July 2025.

Venus did not play singles at Wimbledon and has played just one Grand Slam match this year - a first-round loss to Serbia's Olga Danilovic at the Australian Open.

Williams sisters lose on doubles return

Swiatek beats Rybakina for first title of season

Venus has fared better in doubles in recent years, reaching the quarter-finals in New York last year alongside Canada's Leylah Fernandez.

She has not won a singles match at a Grand Slam since Wimbledon in 2021, where she reached the second round.

However, the Williams sisters still draw huge crowds together or separately, with stands packed out in Cincinnati for their recent return.

Serena, a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion, played what was expected to be the last tournament of her career in New York in 2022.

However, she made her return first in doubles at Queen's in June before being given the final Wimbledon women's singles wildcard.

Venus won her first US Open singles title in 2000, two months after earning her maiden major at Wimbledon.

She beat Serena in the final a year later to defend her title - the first of nine major showpieces the sister would contest.

Venus became the oldest US Open singles player in 44 years when she played at the tournament last year.

She lost in three sets to ninth seed Karolina Muchova and gave an emotional news conference afterwards, saying it was "nice to be free".

In 2011, Williams was diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome, an incurable autoimmune disease with symptoms including pain, numbness and fatigue.

She spoke in 2025 about the impact of painful fibroids - abnormal growths that develop in the uterus - on her daily life.

In the men's draw, France's Gael Monfils has been awarded a wildcard in the final Grand Slam of his career.

There is also one remaining wildcard for the men's singles, which could go to 2016 champion Stan Wawrinka.

The Swiss is also calling time on his career at the end of the year.

Venus may not have won a singles match for over a year, but she is at least appearing regularly - she has played singles and doubles in Washington, Toronto and Cincinnati in the last month alone.

Serena has some decisions to make.

The USTA appears to be holding a singles wildcard open for her, as the All England Club did ahead of Wimbledon.

But does she feel ready to play singles after such little preparation?

Serena's comeback has so far consisted of three doubles and one singles, while the match in Cincinnati was her first in seven weeks after her knee injury.

It seems likely we will see the sisters in the doubles, though - and Serena and Venus may not be the only ones interested in the spaces for next week's mixed doubles event.

Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are back in training after knee and wrist injuries, but have not yet committed to playing in New York.

If they do feel ready to return to singles, then the mixed doubles tournament which precedes it may prove a nice way to ease back in.

title: Poll: Do you think Malik Nabers will play Week 1?

fullText:
New York Giants star receiver Malik Nabers took a big step on his road to recovery on Monday.

Giants' head coach John Harbaugh doesn't believe Nabers is back up to full speed yet, but added that he looked good in what little he did in team periods.

title: Nets' Sean Marks won't change rebuild strategy based off Knicks title
description: Brooklyn Nets general manager Sean Marks won't change the rebuild strategy of the Nets based off the success of the New York Knicks.
fullText:
Brooklyn Nets general manager Sean Marks is in an unique position as the Nets are still rebuilding while waiting for one of its young players to realize their potential. Brooklyn is heading into a 2026-27 NBA season where many expect to be one of the worst teams in the league, but Marks isn't changing his approach, regardless of successful teams like the New York Knicks are.

"Marks, in answer to an ND question about the Knicks back on the day his team introduced its three draft picks, dismissed the possibility of having another team's success change his thinking," NetsDaily wrote on Monday. There are many around the league who wonder how long the Nets are going to rebuild, especially when sharing the same city as a Knicks team that won the NBA title for the first time since 1973.

"(As more than one NBA watcher has noted, the team governor and GM have been like "peas in a pod" when it comes to strategy.)," NetsDaily continued. Marks has been asked multiple times over the course of the past couple of seasons when he would be inclined to change his approach to the roster from patient to a sense of urgency towards winning as many games as possible.

"No, not at all. I mean, we're not, we're not, we're not going to be motivated or less motivated by what somebody else is doing," Marks said to the media in the aforementioned press conference after the team introduced the rookies from the 2026 NBA Draft. "I think all we control is our path. I think we set out on this a couple of years ago, and I think I'm very happy with what the group has done."

This offseason, Marks and the front office made the decision to trade for Minnesota Timberwolves forward Julius Randle and add him to a team where he'll be sharing the floor with sharpshooting forward Michael Porter Jr. and young guard Egor Demin. However, fans that have been supporting the Nets since the beginning are understandably getting uneasy and are hoping for some positive results soon, but Marks is remaining steadfast for now.

title: New York socialist lawmaker takes heat after saying shoplifting results from 'biological need'
description: A New York state socialist lawmaker's framing of retail theft of items like soap being because of a "biological need" was met with swift blowback.
fullText:
A New York democratic socialist lawmaker's referral to shoplifting being the result of a "biological need" is getting swift blowback.

New York state Assemblywoman Emily Gallagher suggested this week that aggressive prosecution of theft of items like soap and toothpaste was wrongheaded, saying the "true crime is that there is such incredible wealth disparity in this city that there are people who can be thrown in jail simply for having a biological need."

"This is exactly the wrong way to talk about crime and poverty. Poverty can help explain why someone commits an offense," former Palm Beach County State Attorney Dave Aronberg told Fox News Digital. "It should matter when prosecutors decide how to handle a case. But poverty is not a permission slip to steal."

Aronberg, who now leads his own law firm, rejected the suggestion that prosecution necessarily means incarceration and pointed to alternatives available for first-time offenders.

Soros Network Rebuilds Progressive Prosecutor Push After String Of Election Losses

"Suggesting that someone who steals toothpaste for the first time is automatically being thrown in jail creates a false picture of how the system actually works. Prosecution does not have to mean incarceration," Aronberg said. "There are diversion programs, treatment, conditional dispositions and other ways to impose accountability without ruining someone's life."

Retired New York Police Department Sgt. Joe Imperatrice, founder of Blue Lives Matter NYC and a retired NYPD supervisor with more than 20 years of law enforcement experience, said politicians should focus on crime victims rather than make excuses for offenders. He also defended the policing strategy Gallagher wants New York City to abandon.

"Broken Windows is a proven theory which holds people accountable for their actions and rightfully so," Imperatrice said. "The tides are turning and everyday New Yorkers are getting sick and tired of this reckless narrative."

"In the very near future we will thank all of these ridiculous so-called 'leaders' for pushing the needle so far left that the great days of the late '90s and early 2000s will be resurrected better than ever before," he added.

Chicago Pol Says Walgreens Should Be Charged With 'First-degree Corporate Abandonment' Over Closure Over Theft

Gallagher, who represents Greenpoint and Williamsburg in Brooklyn, made the remarks Thursday outside Manhattan Criminal Court during a news conference with Court Watch NYC and other lawmakers. She described misdemeanor theft cases involving basic necessities as "crimes of poverty."

"People who are stealing things like toothpaste, people who were stealing things like, you know, soap. And that means if you're stealing those things, you need them," Gallagher said.

Gallagher contrasted struggling New Yorkers with large drugstore chains and argued that wealth inequality was the greater offense.

"And we are choosing to protect billion-dollar companies, like CVS and Walgreens, over the people who are struggling to get by," she said.

Organizers said Court Watch NYC monitored 360 arraignments over four days and found more than half involved misdemeanor offenses.

Crime Is Falling, Officials Say — Victims Claim Reporting Isn't Worth It

Gallagher and her allies also urged Mayor Zohran Mamdani to end "broken windows policing." Mamdani entered office promising to shift some responses to homelessness, mental illness and low-level disorder away from police while maintaining enforcement against serious violent crime.

The NYPD reported retail theft declined 16.3% citywide during the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year. The department attributed the decline to analyzing crime patterns, deploying officers at high-theft locations and conducting sustained investigations.

Aronberg also warned that Gallagher's argument could damage the Democratic Party politically by allowing Republicans to portray the party as unconcerned about crime.

"Democrats should reject the idea that enforcing laws against theft is somehow incompatible with caring about poverty. That is bad policy, and politically it is a gift to Republicans who want to portray Democrats as indifferent to public safety," Aronberg said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Gallagher for further comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers UDFA Jack Pyburn was one of the clear winners of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' preseason win over the New York Jets. Pyburn recorded two pressures, which was enough to catch the attention of head coach Todd Bowles.

Bowles noted that Pyburn has been unable to get the attention he deserves in a crowded edge rusher room. However, he was quite pleased with the statement he made when things mattered.

"He did a heck of a job last night," Bowles said. "He showed up with the lights on. He's a solid player, doesn't get much run with all the other guys playing…he showed everybody who he was."

Bowles on undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks Friday: "He did a heck of a job last night. He showed up with the lights on. He's a solid player, doesn't get much run with all the other guys playing … he showed everybody who he was."

— Greg Auman (@gregauman) August 15, 2026

Pyburn might be able to earn more chances to prove whether he belongs on the 53-man roster if he continues to catch the coaches' eyes like that.

GettyJack Pyburn #58 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Pyburn was undrafted out of LSU, mostly due to questionable physical tools. He showed very short arms at the NFL Combine. They are in the first percentile among players in the NFL. Considering an edge rusher depends highly on arms and reach, this turned plenty of teams off.

Still, he has been able to make a name for himself with a solid preseason. He played 25 snaps, with 16 being rush snaps. He defended the run on seven snaps and had two coverage snaps.

Those were his only two pressures, but he also had two run stops, per PFF. They gave him an overall grade of 71, with his tackling grade being a 74 and his pass rush grade being a 68.7. All three were above average. For what it is worth, his run defense grade was 62.5, which is considered average.

The big issue for Pyburn is that there are limited chances for him to climb the Bucs depth chart. We know that Rueben Bain and Yaya Diaby are going to start on the edge.

The team also signed Al-Quadin Muhammad, who will rotate in with those two. They also have David Walker, who was drafted last year. Walker missed his rookie season due to injury, but has been a presence throughout training camp.

He ran ahead of Pyburn in the preseason opener and looked strong. Anthony Nelson would slot in as the fifth rusher. He is a veteran and could be on the trade block if the Bucs feel good about Pyburn.

Still, last year he was one of their best rushers, so it is hard to see them pushing Pyburn over him. Things open up around the sixth edge rusher.

Mo Kamara is a UDFA entering his third year who is trying to stick around. Yasir Holmes is another rookie UDFA who is not flashing as much as Pyburn. Then, there is Chris Braswell, who has been a letdown since the Bucs drafted him.

If Pyburn does not make a roster push, he appears to be in good position to make the practice squad. He just needs to keep this up.

title: How many games is Giants coach John Harbaugh forecast to win in 2026?
description: How many games did NFL Media's Bucky Brooks forecast New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh to win in 2026?
fullText:
How successful will New York Giants coach John Harbaugh be in his first year with the team next season?

NFL.com's Bucky Brooks forecasts that Harbaugh will win the third-most games among all head coaches leading new teams in 2026.

It is no coincidence that the Giants have captured four Lombardi Trophies under the direction of hard-nosed coaches Bill Parcells and Tom Coughlin. The discipline and attention to detail demanded by those taskmasters brought the best out of blue-collar squads that knocked off heavyweights en route to Super Bowl triumph. Harbaugh's no-nonsense approach could produce similar results for Big Blue, with the Super Bowl-winning coach taking over a roster that has plenty of blue-chip talent on the defensive side of the ball. New DC Dennard Wilson's aggressive scheme will force opponents to contend with a front seven that could rival some of the best groups in franchise history. Although the offense must embrace an error-free approach that relies heavily on the running game and splash plays from quarterback Jaxson Dart, the Giants' ability to force opponents into street fights could make them the team nobody wants to face down the stretch.

Harbaugh has plenty of talent to work with in New York. The Giants have a player at every key position on offense, aside from the offensive line, who is likely to have a breakout year in 2026.

Jaxson Dart has the talent to exceed 3,500 passing yards and 500 rushing yards next season. Cam Skattebo is trending toward a 1,000-yard rushing season, while Malik Nabers is likely to produce like a top-five wide receiver in the NFL. Isaiah Likely ranks among the biggest breakout candidates in the league heading into the upcoming year.

Coupled with their defense, Harbaugh has ample talent to work with as he looks to lead the Giants on a surprise run next season.

The New York Yankees lost their series opener against the Toronto Blue Jays, 3-1, on Friday night.

It was another inconsistent performance from Jazz Chisholm Jr., who recorded one hit in four at-bats and is now 5-for-his-last-35 at the plate.

One moment that stood out during the game came when Chisholm Jr. lost track of the number of outs in the inning.

With two outs, Chisholm Jr. watched the ball in the air after a Yankees hitter made contact. The Blue Jays eventually caught it to end the inning, but Chisholm Jr. reacted extremely late and nearly found himself in a costly situation.

This also isn't the first time this season that Chisholm Jr. has lost track of the outs while on the base paths.

"Wow…how do they continue to put up with that," a fan said.

Someone else added, "Some players you watch daily and just respect. Some players you watch daily and lose respect. Jazz is a player you have to watch daily to really get it."

Another person wrote, "The only way you fix this is by pulling him from the game and benching his [explicit] for the weekend."

"He needs to be benched," a fan shared.

One more fan commented, "Tired of his act."

It's been a tough year for Chisholm Jr., and he'd be the first one to tell you that. He's discussed his struggles on several occasions this season.

"If I knew, I would already have fixed the problem," Chisholm said about his play. "Even when I think I'm getting going hitting, it's still an out. I'm still hitting it right at someone. I can hit it 107 (mph) and still hit it right at someone."

Griner returned Aug. 7 against her former team and helped the Sun earn a much-needed victory over Phoenix. She played 24 minutes in that contest, but her workload has remained something to monitor. The nine-time All-Star was questionable before Thursday's game against the Atlanta Dream. Griner ultimately played, but she logged only 19 minutes and finished with five points, seven rebounds and four assists in a 104-69 loss.

Her remaining on the injury report suggests Connecticut is not yet comfortable declaring the knee issue resolved. Griner has played in only 18 of the Sun's first 32 games this season. Despite the interruptions, she is averaging 13.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks while shooting 52.7% from the field.

Those numbers prove she can still control stretches of games. The larger question is how often her body will allow her to do it.

Griner is not Connecticut's only frontcourt concern. Edwards also could miss Saturday's game because of a left ankle injury. Her presence would become even more important if Griner cannot play.

The Sun already face a significant size and rebounding challenge against New York. Jones remains one of the league's most imposing interior players, while Stewart can score from nearly anywhere on the floor. Connecticut needs Griner's rim protection to discourage drives and contest Jones around the basket. It needs Edwards' mobility and physicality to defend Stewart, rebound and create second opportunities.

Without both, the Sun could be forced to rely heavily on Olivia Nelson-Ododa and Raegan Beers while using smaller lineups for extended stretches.

That approach could improve Connecticut's pace, but it also would leave the team vulnerable on the glass and inside the paint. The Liberty have recently overwhelmed opponents with their rebounding. Giving Jones and Stewart repeated second-chance opportunities would be a recipe for another long afternoon.

Thursday's loss demonstrated how quickly games can get away from the Sun. Atlanta scored 104 points and won by 35. Angel Reese controlled the interior with 15 rebounds, while the Dream repeatedly turned Connecticut's defensive breakdowns into easy scoring opportunities.

Now the Sun must prepare for an opponent with even more proven offensive weapons. New York owns a 21-14 record and recently defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 85-81. The Liberty nearly squandered a 28-point fourth-quarter lead, but Sabrina Ionescu made critical free throws to secure the victory.

The Liberty are dealing with injury concerns of their own. Satou Sabally is out while recovering from lingering concussion symptoms, Leonie Fiebich is sidelined by a foot injury and Ionescu is listed as questionable with a foot issue. That creates at least some hope for Connecticut.

New York, however, still can turn to Stewart, Jones, Marine Johannès and a deep collection of experienced contributors. Johannès recently scored a career-high 27 points while hitting seven 3-pointers in a 111-71 victory over the Las Vegas Aces. Connecticut cannot spend the opening quarter attempting to find its energy. The Sun must defend with urgency, limit turnovers and establish some offensive rhythm before New York begins dictating the game.

Griner's final designation will affect almost every part of the Sun's game plan. If she plays, Connecticut can work through her in the post and force Jones to defend rather than allowing her to roam near the rim. Griner also gives the Sun a reliable target when their perimeter offense stalls.

Her defensive impact might be even more important. Griner's size allows Connecticut's guards to apply more pressure knowing an elite shot-blocker is stationed behind them.

If she sits, the Sun will have to play faster and generate more offense from their guards and wings. Saniya Rivers and Leila Lacan could receive increased responsibility, while Connecticut may rely more heavily on transition opportunities.

Neither option guarantees success against the Liberty.

That is what makes Griner's latest injury update so concerning. The Sun are not merely waiting to see whether one player will be available. They are waiting to learn which version of their team can take the floor.

MORE: Aliyah Boston makes emphatic MVP declaration about Fever teammate

Connecticut's 8-24 record makes a late playoff push increasingly unlikely. That reality should influence how the organization handles Griner.

The Sun would benefit from having their veteran center against New York, but risking further damage to her knee for one regular-season game would make little sense. Griner already has missed 14 games and recently returned from a four-game absence caused by the same injury.

Connecticut must determine whether she is truly ready for another physical matchup. If Griner plays, her minutes could remain limited. If she sits, the Sun will have to find another way to survive against one of the WNBA's strongest frontcourts.

Either way, Saturday's final injury report could shape the entire game before the ball is tipped.

title: How Mets new slugging prospect is striving to fix ‘last glaring hole’ in his game
description: New York Mets outfield prospect Aidan Smith was acquired from the Tampa Bay Rays in the Freddy Peralta trade.
fullText:
BROOKLYN, N.Y. — Mets outfield prospect Aidan Smith knows that he won't reach his full potential until he cuts down on his strikeouts.

This season, before Smith was traded from the Rays to the Mets in the Freddy Peralta deal, the 22-year-old was punching out in a career-high 32% of his plate appearances with Tampa Bay's High-A affiliate. In 49 games, he hit .215 with a .693 OPS.

In 2025, Smith had a 31.2% strikeout rate at the same level while batting .237 with a .719 OPS across 102 games.

JOIN OUR METS COMMUNITY: IT'S FREE ON YOUTUBE!

"I feel like that's the last glaring hole [in my game] and something I can get better at," Smith told NJ.com before his home debut with High-A Brooklyn on Tuesday.

What gives Smith a "really high ceiling," as Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns put it last week, is the rest of his tools. Smith, who is now ranked as the Mets' No. 12 prospect by Baseball America, is an above-average runner and defender. There may be holes in his swing, but he has legitimate pull-side pop.

This is the same prospect who was considered the headliner in the Randy Arozarena trade from the Mariners to the Rays ahead of the 2024 deadline. That year, at just 19, Smith slashed .288/.401/.473 with 11 home runs and a 143 wRC+ over 97 games in Class-A with Seattle and Tampa Bay.

"My first year was a great year and I ended it on a high note with the Rays," Smith said. "Last year, I went a little down, but I learned a lot from it, and really, I think got better on the mental side of the game. It's helping me with my success now."

Smith has made quite a first impression in his first week in a Cyclones uniform. He swatted four home runs in his first six games with Brooklyn while stealing two bases and spending time at all three outfield positions.

Still, the strikeouts have persisted. Smith has struck out 10 times in 30 at-bats over his first seven games in the Mets' system.

"You're never going to be able to be perfect," Smith said, "but if I can at least limit some of that and give myself opportunities to get hustle singles in the infield or draw walks, whatever it may be, I think that's going to really elevate me."

Smith explained that he's working on making better swing decisions. In the cage, coaches pepper him with different types of pitches. Out on the field in batting practice, he approaches each pitch as though he's ahead in a 2-0 count. Those situations force him to be stubborn and wait for the pitch he's looking for in his wheelhouse. When he does get those pitches over the plate, the goal is to put a good swing on them and drive them.

"Swinging at the right pitches and swinging at the right pitches that you're good at hitting," Smith said. "More often than not, you're gonna hit balls you want to hit and those lead to homers."

title: This top Mets prospect grew up a die-hard fan. Here’s why he could be their shortstop of the future.
description: New York Mets shortstop prospect Sammy Stafura was acquired from the Pittsburgh Pirates in the Luke Weaver trade.
fullText:
BROOKLYN, N.Y. — When Sammy Stafura first found out that he had been traded from the Pirates to the Mets in exchange for reliever Luke Weaver, the top shortstop prospect was in the middle of a seven-hour bus ride.

Stafura and his High-A Greensboro teammates were en route to Rome, Ga., scheduled to play the Braves' affiliate the next day.

What followed was a travel nightmare. Stafura sat restlessly for the final four hours of that bus trip only to hop off and take an Uber for an hour and a half to the Atlanta airport. He then flew back to Greensboro and packed up all his stuff before getting back on the road to meet High-A Brooklyn for their road series in Wilmington.

JOIN OUR METS COMMUNITY: IT'S FREE ON YOUTUBE!

It was only then, once he got settled with his new team, that he was able to truly process the news.

Stafura grew up a Mets fan in Westchester County. He still considers himself a "die-hard" to this day, the type of fan that watches the big-league club as much as he possibly can.

Even after he was drafted in 2023 by the Reds in the second round out of Walter Panas High School in Cortlandt Manor, N.Y. and subsequently dealt to the Pirates in the Ke'Bryan Hayes deal last summer, that love for the Mets never went away.

"My room was painted bright orange for the Mets," Stafura told NJ.com ahead of his home debut with the Cyclones on Tuesday. "My mom keeps sending me photos. I was always wearing Mets stuff, always watching the Mets."

Stafura's favorite Mets memory was New York's World Series run in 2015, watching those games with his entire neighborhood. Another was in 2024 when Stafura was watching the Mets' thrilling comeback win over the Brewers in Game 3 of the Wild Card Series from Slovakia, where both of his parents are from. Granted, he didn't get to see Pete Alonso's game-winning home run live.

"The second before Devin Williams was picking his leg up [to pitch], my Wi-Fi just turned off, so I didn't know what happened for like an hour!" Stafura said with a grin. "I was trying to scramble finding Wi-Fi and then I saw the Mets won. It was crazy!"

All that makes the onboarding process much easier for the Mets as they welcome several new prospects into the organization after their trade deadline selling spree. They won't need to spend any time teaching Stafura about the franchise he's now representing.

"I'm going out there and I'll run through a wall for this team," Stafura said. "I'm gonna give them everything I got. This is for the city. This for the town. This for everyone. This for the Mets. So, that's what I'm gonna do. I'm gonna bring the energy and I'm gonna give 100% whatever I got that day."

As much of a dream come true as this opportunity is for Stafura and his family, this 21-year-old shortstop has the potential to make this much more than a feel-good story.

Stafura, who is now ranked as the No. 9 prospect in New York's farm system by Baseball America, was having a breakout summer before he was acquired by the Mets. Over 47 games with High-A Greensboro, the shortstop hit .301 with a 1.021 OPS, 19 home runs and 16 stolen bases. He homered 14 times in the month of July alone.

I asked Sammy Stafura, who grew up a diehard Mets fan, to build his all-time favorite Mets lineup. 

A few of his picks might surprise you…

Watch my full interview with Stafura on Speaking of the Mets right here: https://t.co/cBi3bnq5V2 pic.twitter.com/kXLQ206qix

Don't forget the rest of his tools. As one National League scout put it this week, Stafura's floor is higher than most because of his speed and defense at a premium position.

Stafura flashed both of those above average skills in his home debut at Maimonides Park on Tuesday night. He flew down the line to beat out an infield single in his first at-bat. A few innings later, he knocked a ball down in the hole to his right and fired a strike across the diamond for the out.

"I think the first thing that jumps off the page with Stafura is the defense," Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said on deadline day. "He's got tremendous defensive ability. He's a very good base runner. Can impact the game in a variety of different ways, help you win ballgames in a variety of different ways and clearly he has power as well.

"When you begin to talk about a power hitting infielder who we believe can play shortstop at a high level, that's a player with a pretty high ceiling."

While he's been on fire at the plate for the last few months, Stafura isn't a finished product offensively. The right-handed hitter is striking out nearly 30% of the time with chase and swing-and-miss tendencies that can put him in bad counts. That same scout called those trends "worrisome" and said that he'll need a "better approach."

So, how was Stafura able to explode for such a power surge recently then?

"Stafura is an ambush hitter," the NL scout said. "He went a month where he got into good counts and hit the mistakes."

Clearly the Mets are confident in Stafura's upside. Not only did they part with Weaver, who has another year of team control and would've been a valuable piece of their bullpen next season if they didn't move him, but they reportedly ate $8 million of the reliever's remaining salary.

Asked what's been working so well for him at the plate of late, Stafura singled out his mindset. He's digging into the box looking to do damage — trying to hit the ball hard, far and into the gap — and the results have followed.

"I went up there thinking I'm the best, knowing that I'm the best and that's just the attitude I brought to the field every single day past few months," he said. "I think that's what's helped me a lot in the past few months. And I'm going to keep doing that every single day, going out there, trying to be aggressive, trying to battle. title: Everyone wants to 'tax the rich.' In New York City, it's getting complicated
description: Across the U.S., calls to “tax the rich” have become potent political slogans.  “It seems very simple but the more you dig into it, the more nuances you look at, the more complicated it gets,” said Ga...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Across the U.S., calls to "tax the rich" have become potent political slogans. But even in Mayor Zohran Mamdani's New York, getting the wealthy to pay more isn't playing out as smoothly as supporters hoped.

What seemed at first like an easy idea — slapping a new tax on people who own luxury second homes in the Big Apple but live elsewhere most of the year — has instead created a lot of confusion in the city's notoriously convoluted world of real estate arrangements.

"It seems very simple but the more you dig into it, the more nuances you look at, the more complicated it gets," said Gary Bingel, a state and local tax expert and partner at EisnerAmper, an accounting firm.

It has also prompted pushback from both the city's very wealthy and the merely moderately wealthy.

President Donald Trump, whose gilded Manhattan penthouse could be subject to the tax since his primary residence is now in Florida, said he was looking into whether federal intervention could "avert this disaster, before it is too late."

A group of homeowners sued over the city's rollout of the tax, arguing that officials had not done enough to figure out who would have to pay the tax and instead made it property owners' responsibility. A judge temporarily paused the process this week, but the city moved to appeal, allowing the tax effort to continue until it's sorted out in court.

Securing a new tax on multimillion-dollar second homes, known as pied-à-terres, was an early win for Mamdani in his quest to raise taxes on the city's highest earners to pay for his ambitious liberal agenda.

The so-called pied-à-terre tax would levy a new surcharge on one-, two- and three-family homes valued at more than $5 million, as well as condos and co-ops valued at $1 million or more, if those dwellings are not a person's primary residence.

The idea, according to officials, would bring $500 million to the city's coffers annually, paid primarily by bigwigs who get to enjoy city life but don't pay city income taxes.

That's where things start to get hairy.

It's common for high rollers to place their properties in trusts, obscuring ownership while allowing the property to pass more easily to family members. Limited liability companies can similarly shield an owner's identity, also making it hard for government officials to tell who actually lives in any given apartment.

From there, there are numerous arrangements that can complicate who would be subject to the tax. For example, letting a distant family member stay at a second home without formal documentation, or if someone owns one or more properties and rents them out, but the tenants don't have documentation that the unit is their primary residence.

"Those situations make it difficult to prove people are in there," said Mark Limardo, a partner at the law firm Herrick in Manhattan who focuses on taxes. "The concept is simple, but the ownership rules and the documentation rules have made it very complicated."

City Hall, for its part, argues that it shouldn't be difficult to provide proof that someone actually lives in the city and says that its finance department is experienced in parsing tangled webs of paperwork.

Mamdani, no stranger to razzing wealthy people, debuted the tax with a video singling out hedge fund CEO Ken Griffin by standing outside a Manhattan penthouse the billionaire purchased for around $239 million. The clip sent Mamdani's supporters swooning, but Griffin later said it was "frightening" that a public official would call attention to one of his homes, especially after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in the same neighborhood.

The city then published an expansive online list of property owners who it said could be subject to the tax, listing their names, addresses and property values. The list, which the city is legally required to publish, inflamed tensions between the mayor and the city's wealthy, many of whom argued the roll amounted to doxing or public shaming.

The administration has mailed notices to a much smaller group — about 17,000 properties — that it suspected would be subject to the tax, telling them they could apply for exemptions. Mamdani announced the mailers in a celebratory social media post that read: "If you have a second home in New York City worth more than $5M, check your mailbox when you're back in the five boroughs — because you've got mail."

He later pushed back the deadline for exemption requests following public outcry from people who claimed to have received the letters in error or had trouble navigating the process.

Stewart Sterk, a real estate law professor at Cardozo School of Law in New York, predicted last week's lawsuit wouldn't be the last, saying he expected many of the targets of the tax to file individual cases over denied exemptions, given the vast number of apartments at play and the various arrangements people have connecting them to their properties.

"This is going to be a subject of litigation for quite a while," he said.

Alex Rodriguez: The Dodgers are ‘great’ for baseball
description: While some fans and media believe the Los Angeles Dodgers are ruining Major League Baseball, Alex Rodriguez appears to be a fan of their spending. After admitting he voted in Awful Announcing’s 2026 MLB local TV announcer rankings during an appearance on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN New York, the discussion turned to the…
fullText:
While some fans and media believe the Los Angeles Dodgers are ruining Major League Baseball, Alex Rodriguez appears to be a fan of their spending.

After admitting he voted in Awful Announcing's 2026 MLB local TV announcer rankings during an appearance on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN New York, the discussion turned to the current state of the Yankees, who have been ravaged by injuries and offensive struggles. And while the Yankees remain favorites to win the American League pennant, Kay asked Rodriguez about their biggest potential hurdle to a World Series.

The rich got richer at the trade deadline, when the Dodgers added two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. It reignited conversations about whether the Dodgers are good for baseball or will end up driving owners to continue their push for a hard salary cap during the current labor negotiations. And after Kay held firm that the Dodgers are good for baseball, Rodriguez agreed.

"I think it's great. You and I both would be hypocrites if we said it's not good when we saw what happened in the '90s here in New York, what happened in '09 when Hal Steinbrenner flexed his financial resources to go out and get CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira and A.J. Burnett and the year before we had Johnny Damon," Rodriguez told Kay.

Rodriguez noted that the key to spending money is not making mistakes, suggesting that the $22 million the Yankees spent on outfielder Trent Grisham may have been a mistake. Similarly, the Dodgers shelled out massive contracts for Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz in the offseason, which have yet to pan out.

As a former player, current broadcaster and franchise owner, albeit in the NBA with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Rodriguez is in a unique position to weigh in on the Dodgers. It's hard for Rodriguez to be against the Dodgers flexing their resources considering he signed a groundbreaking 10-year, $252 million contract with the Texas Rangers in 2000 before playing for the Yankees during their peak spending era. It would also be hard for Rodriguez to rant against a salary cap, given that he's an NBA owner with a soft cap.

If the Dodgers win their third World Series in a row after adding Skubal to a star-studded roster highlighted by Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, and Freddie Freeman, the calls for MLB to fix its financial imbalance will grow as they head toward a lockout. But the Dodgers' ability to play the role of the villain also undoubtedly makes the playoffs more compelling, which is why they're still great for baseball.

title: ‘I wasn’t expecting’ – Jalen Brunson reveals what surprised him most about the Knicks’ championship win

fullText:
Jalen Brunson has revealed the unexpected reality of life after winning a championship with the New York Knicks.

Brunson led the Knicks on an incredible run to the NBA Finals, where they defeated Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs in five games.

Nicknamed the 'King of New York', the point guard has suddenly become one of the biggest superstars in American sports.

Brunson has enjoyed the attention since becoming an NBA champion, but it has also caught him off guard this summer.

Even non-basketball fans knew that the New York Knicks winning their first title in over half a century would be a huge moment.

And no Knicks player has received more media attention than Finals MVP and 26-point-per-game scorer Jalen Brunson.

title: New York Yankees vs. Seattle Mariners: Series Preview
description: The Yankees face a trident of right-handers as the scuffling Mariners dock in the Bronx.
fullText:
After three straight series against the Senior Circuit, the Yankees welcome the Mariners to the East Coast. The Bombers had an off day on Monday after dropping the series finale against the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. The Yankees continue to hold serve as they wait for reinforcements to arrive, posting a 5-5 mark over their last 10 games, including an even 3-3 record thus far on the homestand.

The Mariners dock in New York after being swept at home by the pesky and, at this point, must-be-declared-legit Tampa Bay Rays. Seattle's season has not gone according to plan, as star catcher Cal Raleigh has struggled and the club enters play Tuesday sitting at 56-63. The Mariners have dropped four straight and are just 3-7 over their last 10 games.

This series features two night games before Thursday's getaway game, currently scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. Let's dive into which Mariners will be manning the harpoons and which Yankees white whales will be hoping to avoid the trident.

Tuesday: Ryan Weathers vs. Bryan Woo (7:05 pm ET)

Weathers has had a bit of an up-and-down first season in the Bronx. After opening the year looking solid, the month of June was not kind to the left-hander. However, since the calendar flipped to July, Weathers has found his footing again. Weathers currently has a 5-7 record, 3.79 ERA, and a 1.22 WHIP for the season.

Over his last three starts, he has thrown 18.2 innings while allowing just one earned run. That stretch includes six scoreless innings in his most recent outing against the Cardinals at home. Weathers has had his struggles in pinstripes this season, posting a 4.11 ERA at home compared to a 3.35 ERA on the road, but he will look to keep the ball in the yard and continue building on this recent momentum.

Woo is one of the best young pitchers in baseball, featuring a dominant four-seam fastball, excellent command, and the type of arm slot and tunneling that makes pitching nerds drool. The good news? Woo has been two very different pitchers this season.

At home, he owns an ace-like 7-0 record with a 1.96 ERA. On the road, however, Woo is 1-8 with a 6.71 ERA. That difference has held true recently as well. In his last two home starts, Woo has allowed just two earned runs across 13 innings. In his last two road starts, however, he has been roughed up for 10 earned runs in 10 innings. Those splits bring his overall season numbers to 8-8 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.12 WHIP. Expect Aaron Boone to send as many left-handed hitters to the plate as possible, as Woo's platoon splits also favor the lefties. Left-handed hitters have posted a .700 OPS against Woo this season compared to .585 from righties.

Wednesday: Will Warren vs. Bryce Miller (7:00 pm ET)

Much like Weathers, Warren has had his ups and downs throughout the 2026 season. Currently sitting at 8-6 with a 4.18 ERA, Warren's season has felt a bit like a roller coaster. After starting the year in dominant fashion, he has struggled as the weather has warmed. In July, Warren went 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA.

Warren has looked better in his last two starts. Against the Cubs, he tossed 6.2 scoreless innings, and in his most recent turn against the Cardinals, he allowed three runs over 5.1 innings. As one of the backend guys in this rotation, you have to expect some turbulence with Warren, take the good with the bad, and hope he can grind his way to a quality start.

The Mariners will send another power right-hander to the mound on Wednesday, as Miller gets the ball opposite Warren. On the season, Miller sits at 4-6 with a 3.08 ERA. He features an upper-90s fastball that he pairs with a nasty splitter and sweeper. Miller primarily uses the splitter to attack lefties and the sweeper against righties, and both pitches have been effective enough to produce almost identical platoon splits. Left-handed hitters have posted a .630 OPS against Miller compared to .629 from righties.

The good news for the Yankees is that, much like Woo, Miller has struggled away from the Pacific Northwest this season. At home, he owns a 2.09 ERA, while that number balloons to 4.02 on the road. More good news? The summer months have also been less kind to Miller, who currently finds himself in his worst stretch of the season. He has not made it through the sixth inning of a start since July 2nd.

Thursday: Max Fried vs. Logan Gilbert (1:35 pm ET)

The Yankees sandwich Warren with lefties as Fried takes the ball in the series finale. Fried has been steadily building himself back up after missing about two months of the season. Since returning, he has picked up right where he left off and currently owns a 4-3 record to go along with a tidy 2.88 ERA and 0.97 WHIP.

With two August starts under his belt, Fried looks ready for the postseason push. On the first of the month, he tossed 78 pitches of one-run ball against the Cubs before reaching 90 pitches while throwing 6.1 scoreless innings against his former club, the Braves, in his most recent start. I expect the training wheels to come off soon, and might I add that having a left-handed ace take the ball every fifth day is such an awesome thing to get to watch.

While the Yankees show a little spice of life on the mound, the Mariners roll out their third straight hard-throwing righty in Gilbert for the final game. Seattle's front office clearly has a type: tall right-handers who throw hard, get extension down the mound, and command all of their offerings. It is a good type, but with no real wrinkle from one day to the next, hopefully the Yankees' bats can lock in and light up Gilbert.

Gilbert owns an 8-7 record with a 3.42 ERA and 1.00 WHIP on the season. Unlike his other companions, Gilbert has actually been better on the road this year, posting a 2.50 ERA away from home compared to a 4.01 ERA at T-Mobile Park. In his most recent start against the Rays, Gilbert went 6.2 innings and took a tough 2-1 loss after allowing a pair of solo home runs that proved to be the difference. Tampa Bay also worked four walks, a season high for Gilbert.

The Yankees took two of three when they visited Seattle back in late March and early April. Here's hoping for more of the same this time around in the Bronx.

title: Meta glasses banned from courts in England and Wales
description:
Exclusive: Court service says anyone trying to enter buildings with glasses will have them confiscated and returned when they leave
Courts in England and Wales have joined a number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in banning Meta glasses, amid a mounting backlash against what has been described as “spyware”.
Last month courts in New York announced a ban on the controversial glasses, which can record video footage while being worn.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Exclusive: Court service says anyone trying to enter buildings with glasses will have them confiscated and returned when they leave

Courts in England and Wales have joined a number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in banning Meta glasses, amid a mounting backlash against what has been described as “spyware”.

Last month courts in New York announced a ban on the controversial glasses, which can record video footage while being worn.

Now His Majesty’s Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS), which is responsible for all criminal, civil and family courts in England and Wales, has made clear that Meta glasses will be confiscated from anyone entering its judicial buildings.

A spokesperson told the Guardian: “There are clear restrictions on taking images or videos within courts and tribunals which is why the use of Meta glasses is prohibited.”

Taking images or videos in court buildings is prohibited in the UK without official permission and can be prosecuted as contempt of court. While lawyers and members of the public are allowed to enter courts with smartphones, which can record both video and audio, the

HMCTS made clear that no such exception would be made for smart glasses.

A source said: “Users who bring Meta glasses into courts or tribunals will have them confiscated on entry and they will be returned when the owner leaves the building.”

They said smartphones were allowed on the condition they would not be used for recording court procedures.

Earlier this year, a claimant was accused by a judge of wearing smart glasses in the high court and getting “coaching” through them while giving evidence.

Laimonas Jakstys was told to remove the glasses during a case over the directorship of a property company. Raquel Agnello KC, sitting as a judge of the high court, said Jakstys had been “assisted or coached in his replies to questions put to him during cross examination”. Jakstys denied using the smart glasses to receive answers, and denied they were connected to his phone.

HMCTS does not hold figures on the number of incidents of smart glasses being used or taken into courts.

In February, members of the security team for Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, were seen wearing Meta glasses during a high-profile trial in California about social media addiction.

The judge, Carolyn B Kuhl, threatened the security guards with contempt of court if they had recorded any of the proceedings.

New York’s court system said it was banning smart glasses to ensure “individuals cannot surreptitiously record court proceedings”. It added: “No individual possessing smart glasses will be permitted to enter a UCS [unified court system] facility unless they voucher the smart glasses for safekeeping by uniformed personnel while the individual remains in the facility.”

Last year Meta sold 7m pairs of the glasses, which cost between £269 and £469.

Fears about Meta glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent has led to them being labelled “pervert glasses”. A number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in the UK, including Wetherspoons, have banned Meta glasses over privacy fears.

A spokesperson for Meta said the company did not want to comment on the court ban. They said when the glasses were recording a pulsing light was visible to people in the vicinity, and that frequently updated tamper detection technology is deployed to stop users covering this light during recordings.

title: New York Knicks reporter expects Karl-Anthony Towns to sign $45 million contract extension

Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years, playing elite defense against Victor Wembanyama throughout the NBA Finals.
fullText:
Despite not getting the $272 million supermax contract extension from the New York Knicks, Karl-Anthony Towns is likely to stay with the team.

Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years, playing elite defense against Victor Wembanyama throughout the NBA Finals.

And even though the Knicks aren't going to sign him to a lucrative long-term extension, the former All-Star is still expected to stay in New York on a more team-friendly contract.

New York Knicks beat reporter Ian Begley spoke about the future of Karl-Anthony Towns, who is unlikely to get the $272 million contract extension from the Knicks.

He noted that Towns and the Knicks have reason to extend their partnership, with KAT likely getting a $45 million per year contract offer.

"If I had to take a guess, the two sides will reach an agreement. Towns clearly loves New York. Maybe he can make more money with another team next summer (Towns has a $57 million salary this season and his contract has a $61 million player option for 2027-28).

"But why would he leave? He won a timeless championship with his hometown team. Unless the Knicks make an insultingly low offer to Towns, I think they get something done here.

"If I'm using the recent Rudy Gobert extension as a baseline, I could see an extension for Towns starting around $45 million."

Begley added that Towns could make more money as a free agent, but with the current financial restraints placed on teams due to the NBA salary cap rules, staying with the Knicks on a team-friendly deal is a far safer option for him.

"By signing this kind of deal, Towns would obviously lose the opportunity to make more money as a 2027 free agent.

"Given all of the factors at play (the state of NBA economics, teams' approach to the second apron, the Knicks' title), there are reasons for Towns to play it safe and sign an extension.

"Towns leaving New York also would hurt the Knicks. If Towns and the team can't agree on a deal, New York would have to make a significant pivot to find another front-line center. So from the outside looking in, it seems like it makes sense for both sides to figure out a deal."

It's hard to see the Knicks letting Karl-Anthony Towns walk in free agency. Despite all the criticism they received for trading for Towns in 2024, he has rewarded their investment with a championship win.

On top of that, he has become a much better defender than he was earlier in his career, thus providing the Knicks with an elite two-way big who can stretch the floor, an archetype incredibly rare in the modern NBA.

The Knicks know that they can't keep their championship core together for much longer, but they should maximise their time together for as long as possible.

title: Mamdani clashes with Democratic Socialists' push to abolish police and prisons
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails on air, distancing his administration from the DSA's abolition platform.
fullText:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails during a Friday appearance on "The Clay Cane Show," putting distance between his administration and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) platform as political streamer Steven Bonnell, known online as "Destiny," told Fox News Digital that Mamdani would likely govern moderately while helping more radical candidates gain power.

Bonnell said Mamdani's control of a prominent and politically secure office could allow him to build support for other socialist lawmakers without implementing the DSA's most radical proposals himself.

"I think that Mamdani holds a very powerful, very safe office where he can be entrenched for a long time in order to 'hold the door open' for other, (arguably) more radical lawmakers in the future," he said.

Harris Reaches Out To Socialist Mayor Mamdani In Latest Sign She's Shoring Up Support For Possible 2028 Bid

Mamdani addressed his differences with the DSA after host Clay Cane noted that the organization's platform calls for abolishing institutions including prisons, the Senate and the presidency.

"I would say, especially when it comes to public safety, I've been very clear that we have our police force, we have prisons, we have jails [and] the purpose of these is also to ensure that we are delivering safety and justice hand in hand. And what that means is that New Yorkers need not choose between the two," Mamdani said.

He also credited the NYPD with driving down violent crime while emphasizing that public safety should not come at the expense of justice.

"I am proud of our police department for their work in delivering the lowest levels of murders and shootings and even the number of shooting victims in recorded history over seven months over this year," Mamdani said.

Mamdani Walks Back Plan To Increase Nypd Headcount Following Dsa Pressure

The NYPD reported 381 shooting incidents, 462 shooting victims and 149 murders during the first seven months of 2026, the lowest record totals for that period. Major crime declined 6.6% compared with the same period in 2025.

The position contrasted with the DSA's official platform, which describes defunding law enforcement and weakening police unions as steps toward eliminating police and prisons.

DSA co-chair Megan Romer defended the organization's approach to police and prisons during an interview with New Yorker editor David Remnick Monday on "The New Yorker Radio Hour." Romer rejected eliminating law enforcement, while defining defunding as redirecting department money into social programs.

"I am not in favor of getting rid of police entirely tomorrow," Romer said. "I think it means taking funding back and moving it elsewhere, right?"

"It's not communities with cops on every corner. It's communities that have good schools, good jobs, good park systems, good recreation for their teenagers, things like that," she added.

Dsa Co-chair Pushes Back On Soviet Union Comparisons, Wants Prisons To Be 'Less Necessary'

Bonnell predicted to Fox News Digital that the demands of running the nation's largest city would keep Mamdani from applying the DSA's policies, even as the mayor used his popularity to promote other socialists.

"As someone who has to actually govern, though, I don't see him applying any of the more radical DSA positions," he said. "Rather, he'll govern moderately, remain decently popular, market well, then use that position and popularity to promote others."

Republican New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino's office told Fox News Digital that Mamdani's remarks were intended to obscure an agenda that remained central to the DSA.

"Mamdani is politically savvy and understands that DSA messaging on police and prison abolition has been embarrassing and deeply problematic for Democrat candidates heading into the midterms," Paladino said. "As the top DSA figure in the country, he's trying to deploy some smokescreen on behalf of the party, nothing more."

"Make no mistake, abolishing police and prisons is now a baseline policy position for the DSA, regardless of what Mamdani is saying at the moment," she added.

Despite distancing his administration from that platform, Mamdani praised NYC-DSA during the interview for helping elect minority candidates.

"And I think to me, one thing I've appreciated about New York City DSA is that it has been one of the engines behind the creation of a new generation of Black and Brown leadership, the likes [of which] we haven't seen in quite some time," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's office, the national DSA and NYC-DSA for comment on whether the mayor's position conflicts with the organization's platform, but did not immediately receive a response.

fullText:
What a quirk of the MLB schedule: the Braves wrap up a seven-game homestand, go to New York to face the Yankees, then immediately pop back to start a six-game homestand, which begins with the other New York team. Yeesh. To make it slightly sillier, the Braves just visited the Mets before that seven-game homestand began.

At 52-67 despite the season's highest payroll, the Mets are… the Mets. That said, they're not playing terribly right now: 5-3 in August, and 7-7 in the post-All Star Break portion of July, which included a series win over the Braves. For the season, the Mets have largely been marred by being the Mets, rather than anything else. They have the league's third-biggest xwOBA underperformance and its fourth-biggest FIP underperformance. Put those together and it's hard to avoid a miserable season, even if your team is in the top in, say, both xwOBA and xFIP-. What's "changed" since the All-Star Break is a smaller-sample reversal of fortune — the Mets have a massive xwOBA overperformance and are outperforming both their FIP and xFIP. So, y'know, stuff to be aware of in the back of your noggin. The Braves are 4-6 against the Mets coming into this series, so they'll need to sweep 'em to avoid losing the season series to them for the first time since 2017.

On the hill to potentially aid in that endeavor will be Bryce Elder, who brings an 88 ERA-, 108 FIP-, and 99 xFIP- (1.3 fWAR in 126 2/3 innings) to the proverbial table. Elder is in the midst of a silly run over his last four starts, as he's allowed four homers and has a 45/121/105 line in that span — the Braves have won three of those games. Overall, Elder's season has been about inconsistent as his game-to-game slider command. He started out pitching well, but the summer saw a decrease in performance with an especially-large uptick in the rate of homers yielded. One of those clunkers came in his only start against the Mets this year, which was one of his worst: a 2/2 K/BB ratio and two homers allowed in four innings, with the Braves getting blown out.

A random fact: Elder hasn't had a start with an ERA, FIP, and xFIP below 4.00 since May 16… though in terms of ERA, FIP, and xFIP each, he's had six, three, and four starts below that mark, respectively, since that May 16 date.

Opposing Elder for the Mets will be Christian Scott, who is having a nice season at 71/81/89 (1.7 fWAR in just 74 1/3 innings). He's been consistently strong all year aside from a disastrous season debut. The Braves did rough him up a bit in early July (two homers, a 7/4 K/BB ratio in four innings), but he dominated them a couple of weeks ago in New York (7/1 K/BB ratio in six innings), only for the Mets to lose that game as the Braves avoided a sweep behind Chris Sale. title: Mamdani: Democratic socialists ‘going back to what the party used to be’
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said democratic socialists running as Democrats are “going back to what the party used to be.” Mamdani was interviewed for a pre-taped episode of the SiriusXM sh...
fullText:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said democratic socialists running as Democrats are "going back to what the party used to be."

Mamdani was interviewed for a pre-taped episode of the SiriusXM show "Urban View" on Friday. Host Clay Cane asked the mayor if he thinks there are any good contenders for the Democratic nomination for president in 2028. Both Cane and Mamdani dismissed the mayor as an option, as he was born in Uganda.

"I think we have a number of choices," Mamdani said. "I know that people are making their own choices, of whether or not they want to run. What I'm hopeful of is we're seeing a lot of examples of what it can look like to have that focus on the working person. People who understand that affordability isn't just something you say, it's something you have to deliver."

"And that in doing this, we're not running away from the Democratic Party; we're going back to what the party used to be. You think about FDR and La Guardia, you think about the New Deal; that's what the Democratic Party once was," Mamdani continued, referring to former President Franklin D. Roosevelt and former New York City Mayor Fiorello La Guardia (D). "That's what it could be again. And if we want to win, I think that's what we have to become."

Roosevelt and La Guardia led their respective reform agendas to enact New Deal policies aimed at lifting Americans in need of affordable healthcare and housing and facing poverty during the Great Depression of the late 1920s and early 1930s. Both championed policies that Mamdani said on the campaign trail that he would strive toward as mayor.

Such reforms are also popular among democratic socialists who have won a series of recent Democratic primary nominations on the heels of the mayor's victory last year. The victories have put a spotlight on divisions within the party over various policies, including Israel and the acceptance of political contributions from corporations and other political interests.

Democratic strategist James Carville, who notably worked on former President Clinton's 1992 campaign, has been an outspoken critic of the economic populist wave within the Democratic Party. He argued last week to CNN that the party's progressive left is "too hotheaded to know that they're not popular."

Some progressives, however, have dismissed Carville's summation of them and their effect on the party. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who has been the target of some of Carville's remarks, said last week that there was not "much of a choice" with what Carville was saying.

"If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party," Sanders said, referring to Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) and popular left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker.

title: Survey results: Giants fans are feeling the optimism
description: Are NY Giants fans right to be optimistic about their team?
fullText:
The summer is the season for optimism around the NFL, the time when fans of every team allow themselves to indulge in hope for the coming season.

The New York Giants have had a bit more than a week of training camp and are about a week away from their first preseason game on August 15th. Rather than asking about anything specific before seeing the team on the field in a live situation, we wanted to take the temperature of the fanbase as things start to ramp up.

It isn't much of a surprise that the overwhelming majority of Giants fans are either optimistic, or outright excited, about their team. That flies in the face of the national perspective, where the Giants are an afterthought and even outright derided. Even Las Vegas views the Giants as extreme long-shots to make the playoffs this year, with the second-longest odds in the NFC, per FanDuel.

We'll see if the fans or the national perspective is right, but so far the news out of camp has been almost universally positive.

Camp under John Harbaugh has been faster and tougher than what we've seen in recent years from the Giants, with a much higher level of accountability.

The defense under Dennard Wilson has been consistently disruptive and at times dominant. The pass rush has been making the quarterbacks' lives difficult while the secondary hasn't been giving up much separation at all. And while they aren't hauling in all their interception opportunities, the defensive backs seem to be playing faster and more confidently than we saw the last two years.

The defense hasn't been allowing the offense to establish much rhythm or consistency, but we're still getting positive reports out of that side of the ball as well.

Both WR Malik Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo are healthier than many of us on the outside anticipated, and Odell Beckham Jr. has been rounding into form with increased reps. Rookie WR Malachi Fields has produced highlight reel catches with regularity, and the offensive line has looked good as well — despite the pass rush consistently getting into the backfield. It seems that's just a function of the Giants' hyper-athletic front seven, not poor play on the part of the blockers.

There are, of course, fans who aren't drinking the Big Blue kool-aid just yet — And that's fair. After all, the Giants looked amazing in camp and preseason last year, but still managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory on five separate occasions during the season.

We'll see how the good reports translate into the preseason, as well as how the Giants progress over their three preseason games. Last year there were consistent lapses in execution and assignment discipline that were never resolved and became the team's Achilles heel in the season. Even if the Giants don't win their preseason games, we'll see a solid baseline of execution and what issues that crop up be corrected.

title: Amazon responds to Mamdani’s cease-and-desist letter
description: Amazon has responded to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's cease-and-desist letters that went out to 40 major retailers over the sale of "prohibited motorized scooters and e-bikes."
fullText:
NEW YORK (WPIX) – Amazon has responded to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's cease-and-desist letters that went out to 40 major retailers over the sale of "prohibited motorized scooters and e-bikes."

Online retailers, including Wayfair, Walmart, Temu, Target and Amazon, were sent cease-and-desist letters demanding that the stores "immediately end the sale of" prohibited scooters and e-bikes to New York City residents and businesses, according to Mamdani.

If not, the stores could face $2,000 fines as of Aug. 18, Mamdani said Wednesday.

The prohibited nature of these scooters and e-bikes stems from the fact that some of the retailers' products exceed the legal speed limits and wattage limits. Some mopeds don't have proper VINs as well.

The speed limit for e-bikes in New York City is 15 mph. The maximum speed allowance must be under 20 to 25 mph, depending on the bike. Scooters can't weigh more than 100 pounds or go more than 20 mph.

"Let's be clear, these are motorcycles being marketed to New Yorkers as bicycles," said Department of Transportation Commissioner Mike Flynn.

The actions come a week after 17-year-old Gabriel Nacato was fatally struck by an SUV while riding an e-bike in Lower Manhattan. He was on his way from Bensonhurst to fill out summer job applications with a career counselor, Mamdani said.

"The vehicle he was riding is capable of reaching more than 30 miles per hour, a speed that should never be reached in our bike lanes," Mamdani said.

A spokesperson for Amazon told Nexstar's WPIX that the trillion-dollar corporation will be "looking into the products in question" and has no issue working with the mayor and City Council to get it right.

"Safety is a top priority and we require e-bikes sold in our store to meet applicable safety standards and Amazon policies," the spokesperson said.

Target has yet to respond to WPIX's request for comment on the matter.
